label: Draft deliverables
description: Write the product deliverables and their docs (feature.md §1 step 3).

evidence.description: A path:line, a quotation, or a reproduction.

target_id.description: The deliverable, flow, component or unit id this is about.

operation.user:
Turn the issue into product deliverables: who is served, what they can do, and
how we would know it worked.

## The issue

{{.inputs.issue}}

## The docs this phase reads

{{.inputs.working_set}}

**These are paths, not contents.** Open each one with `read_file` before you start. Read the
file as it is now — an earlier state in this phase may have edited it since the run began.

If this conversation already contains an earlier pass, you have read most of these
before. Re-open only what a finding below puts in question, or what another state may
have edited since; re-reading the rest is the largest single cost of a refine pass and
it buys nothing.


## The framing this exploration chose

{{.inputs.framing}}

{{.inputs.residue}}

If those are empty, the catalog already answered the framing question and you
should work from the issue directly.

## What the critique said about your last draft

{{.inputs.prior_findings}}

Where those exist this is a REVISION, not a first attempt. Take each finding and
either fix it, say plainly why it is wrong, or say that you cannot see how to make
progress on it — and record which, per finding, in `responses` below. A finding that
comes back unchanged twice is a finding about this state rather than about the document.

Saying you are stuck is a real answer here, not a failure. If a finding asks for
something this phase cannot produce — a measurement nobody has taken, a decision only a
person can make, a fact that is not in the repo — mark it `blocked` and name what you
would need. Three passes of prose defending a gap costs more than asking once.

## Answer these, in order

1. **Who are we serving?** The user, a developer, support, marketing? Name one
   per deliverable, and name them the way they would describe themselves.
2. **What are the goals?** How does this bring value to that person? Can we
   measure that value — what does success look like, and what does failure look
   like?
3. **How does this feature bring that value?** What is necessary, what is
   sufficient, and what is merely nice to have?
4. **What other features must exist** for this one to deliver its value?
5. **Where does this sit among the features that already exist** — what does it
   overlap with, what does it make redundant, and what would a user expect it to
   do because of a neighbour?
6. **Does it conform to the product principles?** If not, this is an *exception*
   (with the reason, on the doc claiming it) or an *amendment* (the principle is
   wrong). Silence is neither, and phase 8 finds silent departures.

## What a later phase sent back

{{.inputs.returned_findings}}

Where those exist, a phase downstream of this one found the work does not hold up
where they stand — which is why you are running again. That is a different reader
from your own critique: they are looking at what your output made possible, not at
whether it is well made. Fix what they name, or say plainly why they are wrong.
## What the person at the gate said

{{.inputs.reviewer_comments}}

Where that exists, a person read this and sent it back. It is a decision rather than
a critique — they are overriding a recommendation — so what they wrote is the whole of
the reason, and it outranks anything above.
## What to produce

`features` — one entry per deliverable:

```
{ "id": "feature-name",
  "story": "As a [who], I should be able to [what] so that I can [value]",
  "importance": 0.0-1.0,
  "metrics": ["..."],
  "requires": ["other-feature-name"] }
```

Two things to get right in the story. The **who** has to be someone who would
recognise this as their job. The **so that I can** has to name something the
person wanted *before this feature existed* — "so that I can use the new panel"
is the feature wearing a story's clothes.

The metrics must measure the **value**, not the activity. Opens, clicks and
runs-started measure that the feature was reached. Ask which metric would move
if the feature were popular and useless, and do not write that one.

`feature_docs` — one doc per deliverable, on the `docs/_templates/product-feature.md`
template. Each carries its upward link, a **Where this fits** section (serves /
neighbors / depends on / history), and — where the exploration rejected a
reading — a **Framings considered** row.

`standing_amendment` — only when `product/principles.md` is itself wrong. The
gate approves an amendment separately from the feature, so do not fold one into
a doc. It is handed to the critique as its own value, so a doc that cites it does not
also have to prove it exists.

`responses` — one entry per finding in **What the critique said about your last draft**,
in the same order, and nothing at all on a first pass:

```
{ "severity": "significant",
  "claim": "<the finding, as it was put to you>",
  "target_id": "feature-name",
  "disposition": "fixed" | "rejected" | "blocked",
  "note": "what changed | why the finding is wrong | what you would need" }
```

`note` is required for `rejected` and `blocked`. This is the only memory the loop has of
its own passes: the critique reads it to tell an answered finding from a restated one.

story.description: As a [who], I should be able to [what] so that I can [value].

target_id.description: The deliverable, flow, component or unit id this is about.

disposition.description: fixed: the draft changed to answer it. rejected: the finding is wrong, and `note` says why. blocked: the draft cannot see how to make progress on it — `note` says what it would need.

note.description: What changed, why the finding is wrong, or what is missing. Required for rejected and blocked.

inputs.framing.description: The winning framing from the exploration. Absent when the catalog already answered it.

inputs.residue.description: What the exploration leaves behind — the Framings considered rows.

inputs.working_set.description: Paths to the docs this phase reads — its standing docs and the catalog entries that bear on the feature. Open them with read_file: the file as it is now, not a copy taken before this phase started editing.

inputs.prior_findings.description: What the critique said about the PREVIOUS draft. Absent on the first pass. Address each one and account for it in `responses`: a finding that comes back unchanged is a finding about this state, not about the document.

inputs.returned_findings.description: What a LATER phase sent back. Absent on the first pass through. Shapes differ by sender — a review finding carries `severity`/`claim`/`lens`, a design finding raised by acceptance or implementation carries whatever that phase recorded — so read each entry for what it says rather than expecting one shape.

inputs.reviewer_comments.description: What the person at the gate said when they sent this back. Absent unless they did. A decision, not a critique: they are overriding a recommendation, so what they wrote is the whole of the reason.

outputs.responses.description: One entry per prior finding, saying what this pass did with it. Feeds the critique so it can check whether a finding was addressed or restated — the loop's only memory of its own passes.
